newsitem.title: USA: Second U.S. judge denies British nanny bail.
newsitem.headline: Second U.S. judge denies British nanny bail.

text.p: A second U.S. judge has denied bail to an 18-year-old British nanny who stands accused of murdering a nine-month-old infant left in her charge.
Lawyers for Louise Woodward of Chester, England, argued their client has "absolutely no evidence of a past history -- no record -- that she is a threat to the community or the victim's family."

"This woman poses absolutely no risk of flight," defence lawyer Maria Galvagna argued, noting that the British consul was supporting the family and had no intention of issuing another passport for Woodward.

But prosecutor Lynn Rooney told Middlesex Superior Court Judge Raymond Brassard that Woodward "can go to Canada, she can go to Mexico and not even have to show a passport and may not even get stopped."

The judge, after listening to arguments during the 10-minute hearing on Friday, said, "In the light of the seriousness of the offence and in light of the probability ... there is a risk of flight. I deny the bail petition."
Woodward's father Gary, who was among the spectators, dashed out of the courtroom weeping.
Woodward is accused of murdering nine-month-old Matthew Eappen, who died at a Boston hospital last Sunday night from head injuries. On Thursday she entered a plea of not guilty.

Woodward's next scheduled court appearance is on March 6. Prosecutors said it will be up to a grand jury to decide on the severity or degree of the murder charges brought against the brown-haired, blue-eyed nanny.
